title: oidc pending login survives floods and shared proxy ips
description:
GET /api/oidc/login stores a pending state per request in a 1000-entry map (backend/internal/auth/oidc.go addState, evicts the oldest). The per-IP limiter (backend/internal/handler/oidc_limit.go) allows 10 requests per IP, then blocks for 300 s, so 100 IPv4 addresses or one IPv6 /64 evict real pending logins. Behind a reverse proxy without FUSION_TRUSTED_PROXIES all clients share the proxy IP, so 10 requests from anyone block every OIDC login for 5 minutes.
Fix: keep state + PKCE verifier in a signed, HttpOnly, short-lived cookie checked at the callback; drop the server-side map, and the oidc limiter if it is no longer needed.
Read first: backend/internal/auth/oidc.go, backend/internal/handler/oidc*.go, .research/v2-followup/followup_repro_test.go.
May change: backend/internal/auth/oidc.go, backend/internal/handler/oidc*.go and their tests. Not: session/password login.
acceptance_criteria: The two TestFollowupOIDC* tests from .research/v2-followup/followup_repro_test.go, moved into backend/internal/handler/ (adapted if the design renames things), pass; go test ./internal/auth/ ./internal/handler/ passes; goimports clean.

title: Outbound HTTP client: proxy, redirects, rebinding, CGNAT
description:
What/why (backend/internal/pkg/httpc): (P3) a per-feed proxy on 127.0.0.1/LAN is rejected by the dial check because net/http dials the proxy address; (P5) custom CheckRedirect drops net/http's 10-redirect cap, loops until timeout; (P2) SSRF check resolves DNS, then the dialer resolves again (DNS rebinding); (P6) 100.64.0.0/10 not treated as private.
Fix: check the actually-connected IP in `net.Dialer.Control` instead of pre-resolving (closes rebinding); skip the dial check when the client has a configured proxy (admin-trusted; target URL is still validated up front); stop after 10 redirects; add 100.64.0.0/10 to isPrivateOrLocalIP.
May change: httpc/client.go, httpc/ssrf.go. Tests: client_proxy_test.go, client_redirect_test.go, ssrf_cgnat_test.go (+ existing ssrf_test.go must pass).
Evidence: .research/v1-sweep/findings.md (git-ignored). If a repro test is missing from the working tree, restore it from .research/v1-sweep/tests/ (same paths).

title: Feed body parsed with no size limit
description:
What/why: pull/parser.go:87 `fp.Parse(resp.Body)` reads unbounded (gzip-decoded) input; a hostile or broken feed can exhaust memory and kill the server.

title: Puller: report a parse error when a feed's items sit in an unknown namespace
description:
Since gofeed 1.4.1, a feed whose <item>/<entry> elements sit in a near-miss default namespace (RSS 1.0 xmlns without trailing slash, Atom xmlns with trailing slash, xmlns declared on <channel>) parses to 0 items with no error, so the puller records success and the feed silently stops getting items. Decision 2026-10-14 (rf-gofeed-ns): gofeed is right to be strict; refusion reports a parse error instead.

Approach: after a successful parse with 0 items, scan the body with encoding/xml and count start elements whose local name is "item" or "entry" (any namespace; CDATA/text is not counted). If that count is > 0, FetchAndParse returns an error such as "parse feed: N items in an XML namespace the parser does not recognise". A valid feed with no items stays a success. The check lives in a new file backend/internal/pull/namespace.go; parser.go (upstream) gets only the call. Add-feed/discovery is unchanged: such a feed can still be added and shows the error on its first pull.

Read first: backend/internal/pull/parser.go (FetchAndParse), .research/v7-sweep/backend/internal/pull/gofeed_namespace_repro_test.go (cases to cover; git-ignored).

May change: backend/internal/pull/parser.go (one call), new backend/internal/pull/namespace.go, new backend/internal/pull/namespace_test.go. May not change: anything else.

Tests use invented feeds (example.com hosts). No git. Last message: status done/partial/failed, files changed, each check with its output, anything found outside the brief.

title: JSON feeds over 4 KB are rejected as "no valid feed"
description:
gofeed v1.4.0 (backend/go.mod) decides the feed type from the first 4096 bytes and, for JSON, runs json.Valid on that prefix. A JSON Feed larger than 4 KB is cut off, never valid, and Parse returns "failed to detect feed type". Adding such a feed shows "No valid feed found at this URL", and fetching an existing one fails. RSS and Atom are not affected.

Fix: bump gofeed to v1.5.0 (newest; v1.4.2 has the fix, v1.4.1 does not). v1.5.0 also changes author parsing (refusion reads no authors) and xml:base link resolution in Atom; a scratch bump on 2026-10-13 built and passed go test ./... with only the gofeed line changed in go.mod.

May change: backend/go.mod, backend/go.sum, one new test in backend/internal/pull/ with a saved JSON Feed fixture over 4 KB (invented content, e.g. a recipe blog). Nothing else.

title: Pull: items lost with 'database is locked' when many feeds pull at once
description: When many feeds are added at nearly the same time (an OPML import, or a script adding about 25 feeds through POST /feeds), each feed's first pull runs at once. Some 'failed to batch create items' log lines show 'database is locked (5) (SQLITE_BUSY)' or '(517)', and those feeds end up with fewer items than the feed holds. PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000 is set in backend/internal/store/store.go. Error 517 is SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT, which busy_timeout does not retry (inference): a deferred transaction that reads first, then writes, in WAL mode. Likely fix: start write transactions with BEGIN IMMEDIATE, or serialise writers. Read store.go and the item batch insert in backend/internal/store/ first. May change files in backend/internal/store/ and their tests. Write a test that fails on the old code: many goroutines batch-inserting items for different feeds at once into a file-backed (WAL) test database, with no errors and all items stored.
acceptance_criteria: cd backend && go test ./internal/store/... passes, and the new test fails on the old code; goimports -w . and go build ./... are clean

comments.text: Cause: plain SQLITE_BUSY (5) returned at once, not only 517: the FTS5 trigger setup gives a deferred tx a read snapshot first, so its write upgrade skips busy_timeout. Fix: open with _txlock=immediate (store.go). New TestBatchCreateItemsIgnoreConcurrentFeeds failed 5/5 on old code (18-29 of 30 feeds lost items), passes 5/5. goimports, go build ./..., go test ./... clean. title: Sidebar feed row: mark all read button replaces the settings gear
description:
In frontend/src/components/feed/feed-item.tsx, replace the settings gear with a CheckCheck button. It shows only when unread_count > 0.
The button calls useMarkScopeRead from frontend/src/queries/items.ts with feed_id and max_id: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. The backend requires max_id, the sidebar has no list snapshot, and this value means 'everything up to now'.
loadedIds are the unread item ids of this feed already held in the items list caches, so an open list flips them on the spot.
New i18n keys go in all 8 files under frontend/src/lib/i18n/messages/.

Undo by deferring: clicking the button does not call the backend at once. A small zustand store (frontend/src/store/pending-feed-reads.ts) holds feed id -> timer. For 5 seconds the row shows a blue (text-primary) Undo2 icon in place of the count (no countdown), and a sonner toast says 'Marked {count} in {feed} as read' with the app's ghost Button (Undo2 icon + 'Undo') as the action element. Undo from either place clears the timer and the entry. When the timer fires, the useMarkScopeRead call runs; only an error toast remains (apiErrorMessage). Feeds can wait in parallel.

While a mark waits, the feed's unread count is left out of its folder count and the All count (frontend/src/components/feed/feed-list.tsx skips pending feed ids; upstream file, keep the edit minimal).
When the mark commits, the feed's rows already in the open list are pinned with useArticlePinsStore.pinItems(articleListKey(<current list>), ids) before the request, so they stay on screen greyed as read, as the header's mark does.
On pagehide, every pending mark is sent at once with fetch(..., { method: 'PATCH', keepalive: true, credentials: 'include' }) to the same endpoint, using API_BASE from frontend/src/lib/api/client.ts.

title: Article list: a feed check or reconnect doesn't move the list you're reading
description:
What: the open article list must not move while the user reads unless they asked for it. Today two background events reload it, and since rf-stale-pages a reload keeps only the first page and scrolls to the top, so a reader deep in the list loses their place and the next j starts from the first row:
1. A feed check ending. applyPullStatus (frontend/src/queries/pull.ts) invalidates queryKeys.items.all when a run ends. Runs include the list's and sidebar's refresh buttons, Refresh All, adding a feed, and scheduled server checks that the status poll happens to see (usePullStore.running starts a run from idle).
2. A network reconnect. React Query's default refetchOnReconnect reloads active queries (e.g. after the laptop wakes); lib/query-client.ts does not turn it off.

Wanted (user decision 2026-10-12: the app doesn't move what you're reading unless you asked):
- When a check ends or the network comes back, an open list with articles stays as it is: same rows, same scroll, same open article, j/k continue. The "N new" pill (hooks/use-new-articles.ts) shows the count; clicking it reloads and scrolls to the top as now.
- Exception (default, keep it unless it can't work cleanly): if the open list has only its first page loaded and is scrolled to the top, a finished check may reload it in place as today (one request; fresh rows get the existing tint). An empty list keeps reloading on its own as now.
- Lists that are not on screen still get marked stale on check end (invalidate with refetchType "none" for the open one, or equivalent), so switching to them later loads fresh data, first page only.
- Sidebar counts (queryKeys.feeds.all) keep refreshing on check end.
- Explicit actions keep reloading: the pill, filter edits (queries/feed-filters.ts), deleting a feed, OPML import, switching feed or group.

Read first: queries/pull.ts (applyPullStatus, useStartPull), hooks/use-pull-run.ts, hooks/use-new-articles.ts (pill, pullBusy, the page-count scroll reset added by rf-stale-pages), store/pull.ts, queries/items.ts (itemQueries.list has the observer option pages: 1, see its comment and queries/items-refetch.test.tsx), lib/query-client.ts, components/article/article-list.tsx.
May change: those files and their tests. Not backend, not components/ui. Pull-store phases and the pill's "busy" hiding may need a small change so the pill appears once a run ends; say what you changed.

Check and report, don't fix: the list remounts when the window crosses the panes/drawer width (hooks/use-reading-pane.ts), which loses scroll on its own; say whether this bead makes it worse.

Example for tests (invented): a group "Birdwatching" with 30 pages of articles; the reader has 3 pages loaded and is scrolled down; a check ends with 4 new articles.

title: Sidebar: stop re-rendering all rows on URL and ui-store changes
description:

Why it happens (each confirmed in code):
- frontend/src/hooks/use-url-state.ts: useSearch({ strict: false }) with no select, so every caller (each FeedItem, FeedGroup, FeedList, use-sidebar-navigation) re-renders when ?article= changes. Sidebar callers don't need the article id.
- routes/__root.tsx useMatches() and components/layout/app-layout.tsx useLocation() without select re-render RootLayout and AppLayout; Sidebar and FeedList are not memoized; FeedList passes a new feeds array per group each render (getFeedsByGroup).
- app-layout.tsx runs setSidebarOpen(false) on every URL change; zustand notifies all subscribers even when the value is unchanged, and Sidebar, FeedItem and the dialogs call useUIStore() with no selector.
- hooks/use-missing-scope-redirect.ts reads feeds/groups isFetching inside AppLayout, so each mark-read's /feeds refetch re-renders the layout twice.
- components/feed/feed-row-icon.tsx reads the whole pull status (polled every second during a pull) in each of the ~200 rows; it only needs whether its feed is pending.
- hooks/use-sidebar-navigation.ts subscribes FeedList to focusedKey and ringVisible though it only uses them in an effect and a ref.

title: Reading loop: fluid j/k, feed switch and startup
description: Pre-V1 audit (2026-10-12) of the daily reading loop: switch feed or group, scroll, j/k, open article, mark read, plus cold start. One bead per measured or code-confirmed cause. Dependent order: rf-sidebar-rerender first (it masks smaller costs in every measurement).
design:
Method: production build, 200 invented feeds / 47k items, headless Chrome 1440x900, CPU 4x slower, median of 3 runs. 'input' = Event Timing duration, key or click to next paint. The measuring kit lives in .research/reading-perf/ (git-ignored, may be gone): run.sh <binary> <label> [runs] [panes|drawer], env AUTOMARK=open and LATENCY=<ms>.

Baseline 2026-10-12 (panes; drawer within 10 ms):
- j press 112 ms, 19 of 20 presses over 50 ms, 1 of 20 swallowed at a page end.

- Reload to first row 262 ms (592 ms at +100 ms latency); cold start 603 ms (1148 ms).

title: Manage feeds: find why scrolling feels sluggish
description:
Why: scrolling Manage feeds (/feeds) feels sluggish with ~200 feeds. A headless test on 2026-10-12 found no script work while scrolling and no difference with or without tooltips (tooltips need a 600 ms rest to open). So the cost is probably in the browser's own work (style, layout, paint, compositing) or in scroll-linked code, which a headless run does not show. This bead finds the cause and measures it. It does not fix anything.

Read first:
- docs/manage-feeds-speed.md (what was already made faster, how it is measured)
- .research/feeds-perf/README.md and scroll.mjs (the kit and the headless scroll test)

- frontend/src/components/ui/scroll-area.tsx (both the page and the sidebar scroll inside a Base UI ScrollArea, not the window)

Do:
1. Add .research/feeds-perf/scroll-trace.mjs: same app binary and perf.db as the kit, HEADED Chrome (a visible window, needed so paint and compositing are real), /feeds, pointer resting over the rows, wheel-scroll top to bottom and back. Record a Chrome performance trace (CDP Tracing with the devtools.timeline categories) at normal CPU speed and at 4x slower.
2. From each trace report: frame rate and count of frames over 16.7 ms and over 50 ms; total time per category (scripting, style recalc, layout, paint, composite/raster); the top 5 longest events with their stack or source (e.g. ScrollArea scroll handler, a style recalc over N elements). Also: DOM node count on /feeds, and whether any React render happens while scrolling (React Profiler or render counting in a dev build).
3. Try each candidate below as a throwaway stub, measure it the same way, and restore the file afterwards:
   a. the page scrolling natively (no ScrollArea) on /feeds
   b. content-visibility: auto (with contain-intrinsic-size) on group cards
   c. anything the trace points to that is not listed here
   Note what each stub would cost in look or behaviour if made real (e.g. scrollbar style, scroll position restore, keyboard scrolling).

Files you may change: only files under .research/feeds-perf/ (git-ignored). Stubs in frontend/ are for measuring only: back up each file before changing it and restore it exactly; git diff -- frontend must be empty when you finish. Do not change perf.db (copy it like the kit does). No git commands, no SSH, no bd writes.

title: Tooltips: no per-icon setup cost until first hover or focus
description:
Why: Manage feeds (/feeds) freezes ~453 ms on open (4x slower CPU, 200 feeds). Replacing every tooltip with a plain element drops that to ~273 ms (measured 2026-10-12). Each icon button sets up a full Base UI tooltip on render, although most are never hovered. Goal: get most of that ~180 ms back with no visible change.

Read first:
- docs/manage-feeds-speed.md (how the page was made faster, how it is measured)
- docs/frontend-design.md, section 4 (tooltip rule: styled tooltip, never title=)
- frontend/src/components/ui/tooltip.tsx (generated shadcn wrapper: do NOT edit)
- frontend/src/components/common/tooltip-button.tsx, with-tooltip.tsx
- Base UI 1.7 tooltip in frontend/node_modules/@base-ui/react/tooltip/: Root, Trigger, createHandle (one Root shared by many detached Triggers), utils/constants.js
- .research/feeds-perf/README.md (the measuring kit)

Where tooltips are built directly (not via the two wrappers), all must move to the new mechanism:
- components/feed/feed-row-icon.tsx
- components/feed/reorder-controls.tsx (two, one wraps a disabled button in a span)
- components/article/article-appearance.tsx
- components/feed/feed-group-card.tsx: feed error icon, CONTROLLED (open/onOpenChange): on mobile a tap toggles it, only one open at a time
- components/article/feed-error-line.tsx: CONTROLLED the same way (tap on mobile)
Find any others with: grep -rn "TooltipTrigger" frontend/src --include=*.tsx

Step 1, measure before choosing. Two candidate designs:
 A. One shared tooltip per page: Base UI createHandle, one Root + Popup, each icon a detached Trigger with its label as payload. Uses Base UI's own hover/focus/delay logic, no custom event code.
 B. Lazy mount: render the bare control until first pointerenter or focus, then mount the real tooltip around it.
Prototype the cheaper one first (A), stub the rest, and measure with the kit. Pick A if it saves >= 120 ms on visit 2; otherwise try B. Report both numbers if you tried both.

Must not change (these are the reasons this bead exists in this form):
1. Hover: tooltip opens after the same delay as today (Base UI default 600 ms; there is no TooltipProvider) and closes on leave. With B, the FIRST hover must open too, even though the pointer is already inside the control when the tooltip mounts.
2. Keyboard: Tab onto an icon opens its tooltip as today. Mounting must not replace the DOM node: document.activeElement stays the same element and focus is never lost. This is the easiest thing to break with B.
3. Screen readers: every icon keeps its aria-label from the first render.
4. Disabled buttons: the span wrapper still opens the tooltip (tooltip-button.tsx, reorder-controls.tsx).
5. Mobile tap: the two CONTROLLED tooltips (feed error icon on /feeds, error line above an article list) still open on tap and close on a second tap or outside tap, at phone width; only one feed error open at a time.
6. Shortcut hint (<kbd>) and side= placement unchanged.
7. No title= attributes anywhere.

Files you may change: the files listed above, new files under frontend/src/components/common/, tests next to the files (*.test.tsx, the repo's convention), docs/manage-feeds-speed.md (tooltip line: the new numbers and design) and docs/frontend-design.md section 4 (only if the tooltip rule's wording must change). Leave components/ui/ alone. Keep edits in upstream files (feed-group-card, feed-error-line, article-appearance) to the smallest change. No git, no SSH.

  - Tab to it -> label appears; document.activeElement is the same node before and after the tooltip mounts
  - disabled TooltipButton -> hover opens the label

title: Keep the sidebar mounted when switching between Manage feeds and article lists
description:
Why: FeedsPage (frontend/src/routes/feeds.lazy.tsx) and ArticlePage (frontend/src/components/article/article-page.tsx) each wrap themselves in <AppLayout>. React therefore tears down and rebuilds the whole layout on every switch between them: the sidebar with every feed, plus the keyboard and pull hooks. That costs ~255 ms on a 4× slower CPU and resets the sidebar's scroll position.

- /login must not get the layout.
- ArticlePage passes readingPane to AppLayout. Keep that working, for example by deciding it from the current route inside the shared layout, or by another small approach.
- Prefer a choice that changes few upstream files and renames no route files. This fork keeps upstream files minimal so upstream merges stay easy (.agents/AGENTS.md). If that's impossible, stop and report the options.
- app-layout.tsx now also mounts usePrefetchFilterViews (rf-filter-hoist, c5672c6): keep it in the shared layout. Mounted once, it prefetches once per app load; that is intended.

title: Manage feeds: one filter dialog and one data read per page, not per row
description:
Why: each feed row on Manage feeds mounts its own FeedFilterControl. That means its own closed FilterDialog, 2–3 tooltips, two query subscriptions (useFeedFilters, useHiddenCounts) and one mutation hook. With 200 feeds this costs ~270 ms of the ~730 ms freeze (4× slower CPU). It also causes a second ~115 ms freeze when the hidden counts arrive and every row redraws.

What:
- Lift the dialog and the data reads to the page (or the group list). The page mounts one FilterDialog for "the feed being edited", reads useFeedFilters and useHiddenCounts once, and passes each row its filter and counts as props.
- The row keeps the same look and behaviour: the filter button with its label and hidden count, the "hidden by global" note, the on/off switch, and the same tooltips.
- Clicking a row's filter button opens the single dialog for that feed.
- The global filter row (GlobalFilterRow) keeps its own dialog.
- Where it costs nothing, wrap the row in React.memo so a counts change redraws only rows whose values changed.

title: Deleted feed/group URL opened directly shows an empty list
description:
What/why: opening /feeds/<id>/<filter> or /groups/<id>/<filter> for a feed or group that no longer exists (old bookmark, typed URL, another tab deleted it) shows an empty or error list instead of landing on /unread. The route guards (routes/feeds_.$feedId*.tsx, routes/groups.$groupId*.tsx) only check the id is a positive integer; they don't know which ids exist.

No redirect while loading or on a fetch error. Must not bounce a feed just created and navigated to before the list refetches: check useCreateFeed / add-feed flow updates the cache first, and handle it if not. Keep route files (upstream) untouched.

title: Global filter: storage, combine with feed filter, endpoints
description:

- Migration 904_global_filter.sql: table global_filter with id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK (id = 1), the same columns as feed_filters minus feed_id, and action fixed to 'remove' by a CHECK.
- Combining: activeMatcher becomes activeMatchers(feedID), returning the global and the feed matcher (either may be missing). Hidden = any matcher hides. recomputeFilterTx and MarkFilteredInputs use it.
- RecomputeAllFilters: loops over the feeds, one transaction each (reusing recomputeFilterTx), so no transaction holds the write lock for long. It returns the total number of hidden articles.
- Store, in new file store/global_filter.go: get, upsert, set enabled, delete. Each runs RecomputeAllFilters after its own transaction commits. Upsert rejects action 'keep' with ErrInvalid.
- Global preview: the draft rule runs over the latest 300 articles across all feeds, with no saving. It returns {checked, hidden, items: [{id, feed_id, feed_name, title, pub_date, hidden}]}.
- Per-feed PreviewFilter also applies the saved global filter if it is on: each item gets global_hidden. The response gets global_hidden, a count of the articles the global filter hides, kept apart from the draft rule's own hidden count.
- Endpoints, in new file handler/global_filter.go, following api-conventions:
  - GET /global-filter (null when none)
  - PUT /global-filter
  - PATCH /global-filter {enabled}
  - DELETE /global-filter
  - POST /global-filter/preview
- Mirror the new shapes in frontend/src/lib/api/types.ts and add api calls in lib/api/index.ts. No UI.
- docs/feed-filter.md: a short "Global filter" section with the epic's decisions (link, don't restate the code).

title: Global article filter (remove, all feeds)
description: One filter that hides articles across all feeds, next to the per-feed filters from rf-feed-filter (docs/feed-filter.md). Edited from the top of Manage feeds with the same dialog.
design:
2026-10-11 decisions:
- One global filter, Remove only (a global Keep would hide almost everything).
- Own one-row table global_filter, not a nullable feed_id in feed_filters (that is the primary key; changing it means rebuilding the table and touching every query).

title: Mark all as read: cover the whole feed/folder, not just loaded rows
description:
The list header "mark all as read" button (frontend/src/components/article/article-list.tsx, handleMarkAllAsRead) sends only the ids of rows already loaded, so unread items on later pages stay unread. Same in feed, folder and All views. Upstream has the same bug.

description:

- New package internal/airank. Ranker.Start(ctx) runs only when the key is set; started in main.go next to the puller. Every 5 minutes:
  - Skip the run when the global note is empty, or when 1,000 item_scores rows already have scored_at today.

title: AI ranking: score articles in chosen feeds against the reader's notes
description:
What: score articles of chosen feeds against notes the user writes (Love / Like / Skip), show the group as a badge, offer a "Ranked" sort.
Why: an Inoreader-style "sort by magic" for a single-user reader. Popularity data from other users doesn't exist here, so a model judges fit with the user's notes (2026-10-11).
Code lives on branch ai-rank in worktree ../refusion-ai-rank (dev DB copy dev-ai-rank.db there), so the feature can be dropped by deleting the branch. Merge main into the branch before each bead starts.
design:
Decisions (2026-10-11), after tests in .research/ai-rank/ (git-ignored)

Model and request
- TypeSafe Jev (decision model) via OpenRouter's Decisions API (POST https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions), pinned typesafe/jev-1.13 (FUSION_AI_MODEL overrides).
- Pluggable (2026-10-11, rf-rank-endpoint): FUSION_AI_URL, any service speaking the SystemOne score shape; default OpenRouter's production /api/v1/systemone. Jev was the quickest way to test, not a commitment. On when FUSION_AI_API_KEY or FUSION_AI_URL is set. Chosen over DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on 30 Hacker News items: same top and bottom, ~5x cheaper (~$0.00002/article), 2 s vs 40-58 s, stable (+-0.27), no JSON or ID mix-ups; it returns no reason text.
- One request per article. state = {reader_note, feed_note, article: {feed, title, text}}; text = strip_html(content), first 2,000 characters. Question "worth", type score, instructions: "How worth reading is this article for this reader? Judge by reader_note; feed_note, when present, refines it for this feed and wins where they differ." Levels low to high: 0 "matches something the note says to skip", 1 "the note says nothing about it either way", 2 "relevant or closely related to a liked topic", 3 "directly about something the reader loves". Store the 0-3 score and the confidence.
- Jev reads state in order (2026-10-11 live test: article first raised middle scores 0.4-1.0). Request is built from structs, reader_note first; rank_key includes a request version, bumped on any request change.
- Feed-note test (9to5Mac, 2026-10-11): deals moved Neutral -> Skip as asked; "Neutral at best" wording pushed items to ~0.4 (Skip). Placeholders should show clear rules, not "at best". Not yet seen: a desktop-Mac item reaching Love.

Notes and switches
- Global note in Settings -> AI ranking; optional per-feed note plus the "Rank with AI" switch in the edit-feed dialog (gear -> Advanced; not in add-feed). Each note at most 1,000 characters. Empty global note = nothing is scored. Switch off by default.
- Editing a note (or changing the model) rescores unread articles from the last 7 days; old scores stay visible until replaced.

Groups and sort
- Groups by nearest level: Love >= 2.5, Related >= 1.5, Neutral >= 0.5, Skip < 0.5. The backend owns the boundaries and sends rank_group.
- Unscored counts as Neutral: not scored yet, older than 7 days when the switch went on, unranked feeds, feeds whose switch was turned off.
- Ranked sort: Love, Related, Neutral, Skip; newest first inside each group. Badges only on Love (strong) and Related (soft).

Without a key or URL
- Nothing runs or is sent. UI looks like today except the Settings tab, which explains the feature and how to turn it on. Stored notes and switches are kept.
- Code: all UI in components/ai-rank/, gated by one hook (useAiRank) reading GET /api/ai-rank/status; upstream files only get the lines that place the components.

Errors
- Status in the Settings tab, plus a red line in the article list (feed-error-line pattern) when the view has a ranked feed or Ranked sort is on.
- Codes: 401 key_rejected (stop until restart); 402 no_credit; 404 not_found; 429/5xx/network unavailable (all retry every 5 min); refused (a run skipped articles and scored none: the service refused every request; retry every 5 min); cap_reached (grey, wait for tomorrow). One bad article counts as skipped, not an error.

Limits and data
- Every 5 min, up to 200 articles per run, 5 at a time, at most 1,000 per day.
- Leaves the server: title, feed name, 2,000 characters and both notes, to OpenRouter and TypeSafe.

Docs
- README "What refusion adds": optional, does nothing without FUSION_AI_API_KEY, what it sends. .env.example: both variables. docs/ai-rank.md (fork): why, these decisions, gotchas, live-state commands. In-app explainer at the top of the Settings tab.

Later / parked
- Later: thumbs up/down corrections as examples. Parked: open-weight Jev variants (Open-Jev, JevK5) so nothing leaves the server.

description:

Why: see epic rf-pull-refresh (read its design field first).

Backend

- handler/pull.go: GET /api/pull/status also returns last_item_id (MaxItemID). New GET /api/pull/new-count?after_id=&feed_id=&group_id= -> {count}. It lives under /pull because a static /items/x route next to /items/:id is risky in gin. Bad or missing after_id -> 400. Register it in SetupRouter next to the other pull routes.

This covers the pill and runs that end with a list reload. Switching view or the first load of a view: no tint. ArticleItem gets one optional prop (e.g. isFresh) that adds the class.

title: Pull: pull-to-refresh in the sidebar, progress, Shift+R
description:
What: track which feeds are being fetched, expose it, and show it at the top of the sidebar with a pull-down gesture that checks all feeds.
Why: see epic rf-pull-refresh (read its design field first).
Read first: backend/internal/pull/puller.go, backend/internal/handler/handler.go (SetupRouter, the puller interface), backend/internal/handler/feed.go (refreshAllFeeds, createFeed), docs/api-conventions.md, frontend/src/components/layout/sidebar.tsx, components/feed/feed-list.tsx, hooks/use-keyboard.ts, components/layout/shortcuts-dialog.tsx, queries/feeds.ts, lib/api/index.ts, lib/i18n/messages/en.ts.

Backend
- New pull/progress.go: a mutex-guarded count per feed ID of queued-or-running manual fetches, plus a running total of new items saved (any source). Puller.PullStatus() returns the pending IDs (sorted) and that total. Puller.RefreshFeeds(ids) marks them pending synchronously (skips ones already pending), returns how many it queued, then fetches them in a goroutine under the existing semaphore, each un-marked when done even on failure, then Wake(). Use context.Background with a cap like refreshAllTimeout.
- puller.go (upstream, keep it to a few lines): a progress field (zero value must work, New unchanged); RefreshFeed marks its feed pending at its very start and un-marks it in a defer (so add-feed and OPML import show); pullFeed adds newCount to the total after BatchCreateItemsIgnore succeeds.
- New handler/pull.go: GET /api/pull/status -> {pending: [ids], new_items: n}; POST /api/pull, body {feed_id?, group_id?} -> resolve feed / group's feeds / all feeds, skip suspended, RefreshFeeds, 202 {queued: n}; unknown feed or group -> 404. Get the extra methods by type-asserting h.puller to a local interface (don't widen New's interface: test fakes implement it); if absent, internal error. Follow docs/api-conventions.md for response shape. Register both routes in SetupRouter (handler.go) next to the feed routes.
- Test (new, must fail on the old code): pull/progress_test.go, real store and an httptest feed server serving two feeds: RefreshFeeds -> PullStatus lists both right away -> after completion pending is empty and new_items equals the items served. Reuse helpers in pull/puller_test.go.

Frontend (new files where possible)
- lib/api/pull.ts: pullAPI.status / pullAPI.start({feed_id?, group_id?}) and their types (export the shared client from lib/api/index.ts if it isn't). Mirror shapes exactly.
- queries/pull.ts: usePullStatus (refetch every 1000 ms while pending is non-empty, else 60000 ms) and useStartPull (refetches status on success).
- store/pull.ts (small zustand store) + hooks/use-pull-run.ts, called once in app-layout.tsx so it runs even when the phone drawer is closed: pending empty->non-empty starts a run (remember new_items, total = peak pending count); done = total - current pending; non-empty->empty ends it: invalidate feeds and items queries, show the result for 1500 ms. new_items changing with no run: invalidate the feeds list only (unread counts). queued 0 with nothing pending: show "Nothing new".
- hooks/use-pull-to-refresh.ts: given a scroll element, report pull distance and armed state, call onRefresh on release past the threshold (~64 px shown, with resistance). Touch: start only at scrollTop 0; non-passive touchmove, preventDefault while pulling. Wheel: a gesture starts after >=200 ms with no wheel events and counts only if scrollTop is 0 at that moment; sum upward deltas (deltaMode lines x16); "release" = 150 ms with no wheel event. Set overscroll-behavior-y: contain on the scroll element (stops Chrome Android's page reload).
- components/feed/pull-indicator.tsx: top of the sidebar, under the header. Height follows the pull; arrow turns when armed; then spinner + "Checking 12 / 48" (total > 1) or "Checking..."; then the result. Hook up in sidebar.tsx around <FeedList/>; find the ScrollArea viewport via [data-slot=scroll-area-viewport] inside a wrapper ref (don't edit components/ui/).
- Shift+R in use-keyboard.ts starts a pull of all feeds; list it in shortcuts-dialog.tsx.
- queries/feeds.ts: useRefreshFeeds calls pullAPI.start({}) and drops its early invalidation; useCreateFeed and the OPML import success path refetch pull status.

title: Fetch progress: pull to refresh, progress, new-article pill
description:
What: show when feeds are being fetched, and let the user trigger fetches by pulling down.
Why: today every fetch runs unseen; "Refresh All" reloads before anything is fetched, and a new feed shows 0 articles until a page reload (2026-10-10).
design:
Decisions (2026-10-10), after reading yarr (status counter polled every 500 ms, sidebar footer "Refreshing (N left)", per-feed error icon):
- Pull down in the sidebar = check all feeds. Pull down in the article list = check that view (all / folder / feed). No pull on Starred.
- Texts: "Pull to check for new articles" -> "Let go to check <scope>" -> "Checking 12 / 48" -> "3 new articles" / "Nothing new" (~1.5 s).
- Progress lives in the pull spot at the top of the pane; no bottom bar. OPML import, add feed and refresh-all show the same top-of-sidebar progress without a pull.
- Scheduled fetches show no progress; they only reload unread counts.
- Keys: r = check the current view, Shift+R = check all feeds. No confirm dialog.
- Trackpad pull is built on wheel events: only a pull that starts while the pane already rests at the top counts (avoids firing on momentum scroll).
- A background fetch never reflows an open article list: a "N new articles" pill; click reloads and scrolls to top; new rows get a tint fading over ~2 s (sort is by pub_date, so some land mid-list). Empty list: new articles just appear.
- Status is polled: 1 s while fetching, 60 s otherwise. No push.
- Mark-all-read marks only loaded IDs, so unseen new articles stay unread.

title: article list: yarr-style infinite scroll, native scroller, memoized rows
description:
Why: new pages land mid-fling (list jumps) and every loaded row re-renders on each page/toggle/selection (stutter that grows with the list). yarr (nkanaev/yarr, src/frontend/js/pages/App.vue refreshItems/loadMoreItems/itemListCloseToBottom, directives/scroll.ts) waits until scrolling stops.

On the scroll div, a scroll listener debounced 200 ms calls fetchNextPage() when the viewport is within ~70px of the bottom and hasMore && !isLoadingMore && !isFetchNextPageError, and only when articleLoading === "scroll". title: Full article: per-feed setting to always load full content
description:
What: a per-feed switch "Always load full article", stored on the server. When it is on, opening an article from that feed fetches the full content automatically, as if the user pressed `w`. Why: some feeds ship only a teaser, so the user presses `w` on every article.

Backend:
- New migration backend/internal/store/migrations/900_feed_full_content.sql: `ALTER TABLE feeds ADD COLUMN full_content INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`. INTEGER matches the existing flags (suspended, unread) because SQLite has no real boolean type. Fork migrations use 900+ so they never share a version number with upstream's 007+ (schema_migrations keys on the number alone).
- model.Feed gains `FullContent bool json:"full_content"`. Read it in both feed SELECTs in store/feed.go. CreateFeed takes it; UpdateFeedParams gains `FullContent *bool`.
- handler/feed.go: createFeedRequest gains `FullContent bool json:"full_content"`; updateFeedRequest gains `FullContent *bool json:"full_content"`. Update every CreateFeed caller, tests included.

Frontend:

Pressing `w` (or the button) switches back to the feed text and must not re-fetch for that article. A failed fetch keeps the feed text and shows the existing toast. title: Pull: make http(s) URLs in media:description clickable
description:
What/why: media:description (YouTube and other media-RSS feeds) is plain text. mediaDescription in backend/internal/pull/mediadesc.go escapes it and turns newlines into "
\n", so URLs in it show as plain, unclickable text. Wrap them in . The frontend sanitizer (frontend/src/lib/content.ts, sanitizeAnchors) already keeps and adds target="_blank" and rel="noopener noreferrer"; no frontend change. Read first: backend/internal/pull/mediadesc.go, mediadesc_test.go. Build, in mediadesc.go only: - Find URLs in the RAW text (after trim and \r\n -> \n, before escaping) with regexp `https?://[^\s<>"]+`. Strip trailing .,;:!?'" from each match, and a trailing ) when the match has no "(". The stripped characters stay in the text after the link. - Build the output piece by piece: html.EscapeString each text piece; each URL becomes ESC with ESC = html.EscapeString(url). Then "\n" -> "
\n" as today. Escape per piece, never linkify already-escaped text (& in query strings would double-escape). - Only http:// and https:// match; bare domains (goo.gle/x) stay text. Test: extend the existing test in mediadesc_test.go (no new test function unless it reads better). Add to entry A's text (invented): "See https://example.test/a?b=1&c=2. and (https://example.test/x)" -> Content contains https://example.test/a?b=1&c=2. -> Content contains (https://example.test/x) Keep A's existing script/&/
assertions passing. Must fail on the current code. May change: backend/internal/pull/mediadesc.go, mediadesc_test.go. Nothing else. No git, no SSH, no bd. Comments at most 3 lines, why not what. Out of scope: links in other content, bare domains, backfill of stored rows.

title: Add opt-in panes layout
description:
# Brief 2: opt-in panes layout (feeds | article list | article)

## Why
Today an opened article slides in as a drawer over the list. Users can opt into a
3-column layout instead: the article shows in a pane next to the list. The drawer
stays the default. This repo is a fork that merges upstream often: put new code
in new files and keep edits to existing files small.

## Read first
- Root `AGENTS.md` (repo rules), `.agents/AGENTS.md` (fork rules)
- `frontend/src/components/article/article-view.tsx`: `useArticleViewState()` and
  `ArticleView`, already shared by the drawer
- `frontend/src/components/article/article-drawer.tsx`, `article-page.tsx`,
  `components/layout/app-layout.tsx`, `store/preferences.ts`,
  `components/settings/settings-dialog.tsx` (the auto-mark-read row)

## Files allowed
- `frontend/src/store/preferences.ts`
- `frontend/src/components/settings/settings-dialog.tsx`
- `frontend/src/components/article/article-pane.tsx` (new)
- `frontend/src/components/article/article-page.tsx`
- `frontend/src/components/layout/app-layout.tsx`
- `frontend/src/components/article/article-item.tsx`
- `frontend/src/lib/i18n/messages/*.ts` (all 8 locales)
- `docs/frontend-design.md`
Touch nothing else (not `settings-sync.ts`, not the backend, not `components/ui/`).
No git commands.

## What to do
1. **Preference.** In `preferences.ts` add `readingLayoutOptions = ["drawer", "panes"]`,
   type `ReadingLayout`, default `"drawer"`, `setReadingLayout`, and normalise it in
   `merge` the same way `autoMarkRead` is (an older persisted blob lacks the key).
   Add it to `partialize`. It is per device: never sent to the server.
2. **Settings row.** In `settings-dialog.tsx`, add a "Reading layout" select directly
   below the auto-mark-read row, same markup. Its `onValueChange` calls
   `setReadingLayout(v)` only: no `applySetting`, no `beginChange`, no PATCH.
3. **ArticlePane** (`article-pane.tsx`). Calls `useArticleViewState()` once. When
   `state.isOpen` is false, or the article is not loaded yet, it shows a centred
   empty state: lucide `BookOpen` icon (muted, about 48px) and the text
   `article.pane.empty`. Otherwise `<ArticleView state={state} variant="pane" />`.
   Root: `<section className="flex h-full min-w-0 flex-1 flex-col">`.
4. **Layout switch.** In `article-page.tsx`: `panes = readingLayout === "panes" && !isMobile`
   (`useIsMobile`). When `panes`, render inside `AppLayout` a row: the `ArticleList`
   in a `w-[400px] shrink-0 border-r` column, then `<ArticlePane />`. Otherwise render
   exactly what it renders today. Pass `readingPane={panes}` to `AppLayout`, which
   skips `<ArticleDrawer />` when `readingPane` is true. Every other page keeps the
   drawer (search can open an article from any page).
5. **Scroll into view.** In `article-item.tsx`, when the row becomes selected, call
   `scrollIntoView({ block: "nearest" })` on its root element (ref + effect).
   This applies in both modes.
6. **Text.** New keys in all 8 locale files, translated properly and in the style of
   each file (e.g. `de.ts` writes umlauts as plain letters):
   `settings.readingLayout.label` "Reading layout",
   `settings.readingLayout.description` "Drawer opens articles over the list. Panes shows them in a column beside it (wider screens only).",
   `settings.readingLayout.drawer` "Drawer", `settings.readingLayout.panes` "Panes",
   `article.pane.empty` "Select an article to read".
7. **Docs.** `docs/frontend-design.md`: in section 3 the `article` row says "Opened
   article (drawer or reading pane)"; in section 4 Desktop, say the article opens in
   the drawer or, with the panes layout, in a column beside a 400px list; in
   section 5, note that the reading layout is the one preference kept per device
   and never synced. Change only those sentences.

## Hard constraints
- At any moment exactly one of `ArticleDrawer` or `ArticlePane` is mounted. Both
  call `useArticleViewState()`, which registers keyboard navigation; two mounted
  means `j` skips articles.
- Do not change `article-view.tsx`, `article-drawer.tsx` or any hook.
- Drawer mode must look and behave exactly as before.
- No new dependencies. No tests of wording.

## Checks (run in `frontend/`, all must pass)
- `pnpm run typecheck`
- `pnpm test`
- `pnpm run check:i18n`
- `pnpm build`

## Report back
- The checks' last lines.
- Anything you had to do differently from this brief, and why.
acceptance_criteria: In frontend/: pnpm run typecheck, pnpm test, pnpm run check:i18n, pnpm build pass; exactly one of ArticleDrawer/ArticlePane mounted; click-through in both modes.

title: Split ArticleDrawer into state hook + view
description:
# Brief 1: split ArticleDrawer into state hook + view (no visible change)

## Why
A later change adds an inline reading pane next to the article list. It must show
the same article UI as the slide-out drawer. This step only separates logic from
presentation so both can share it. Nothing may change for the user.

## Repo
This repo, frontend in `frontend/`. Read `AGENTS.md` (root) first.

## Files allowed
- `frontend/src/components/article/article-drawer.tsx` (edit)
- `frontend/src/components/article/article-view.tsx` (new)
Touch nothing else. No git commands.

## What to do
1. In `article-view.tsx`, export a hook `useArticleViewState()` that contains,
   moved unchanged, everything `ArticleDrawer` computes today before its `return`:
   URL state, `useArticleList`, mutations, read-state pins, the article/readArticle
   resolution, `useAutoMarkRead`, all handlers, and `useArticleNavigation`.
   Keep every existing comment, word for word, next to the code it explains.
   It returns what the JSX needs (article, readArticle, canToggleRead, feed,
   bookmark, starred, safeArticleLink, the handlers, goToNext/goToPrevious/
   hasNext/hasPrevious, and a `close()` that calls `setSelectedArticle(null)`).
2. In the same file, export `ArticleView({ state, variant })` with
   `variant: "drawer" | "pane"`. It renders the header, content and footer
   exactly as the drawer's JSX does today, and returns `null` when there is
   no article. `SheetTitle` (sr-only) renders only for `variant === "drawer"`.
   `getLinkDomain` becomes a module-level function in this file.
3. `ArticleDrawer` becomes a thin shell: it calls `useArticleViewState()` at its
   top level (outside the Sheet), then renders the same `<Sheet>`/`<SheetContent>`
   as today with `<ArticleView state={state} variant="drawer" />` inside.

## Hard constraints (these are the bugs to avoid)
- The hook must run in `ArticleDrawer` itself, never inside `SheetContent`.
  Today the logic runs while the drawer is closed; `useAutoMarkRead` relies on
  seeing its target go to `null` when the article closes. Moving the hook inside
  the Sheet would unmount it on close instead and change that behaviour.
- `useArticleNavigation` must still be called exactly once by the drawer path,
  with the same `enabled: selectedArticleId !== null` and the same callbacks.
  A second call registers a second keydown handler and `j` skips articles.
- No renames of i18n keys, CSS classes or props; no new dependencies;
  no behaviour or styling changes; no "while I'm here" cleanups.
- Comments only where the repo's rules say so (`AGENTS.md`, Code Standards).

## Checks (run in `frontend/`, all must pass)
- `pnpm run typecheck`
- `pnpm test`
- `pnpm run check:i18n`

## Report back
- The checks' last lines.
- Any place you could not move code unchanged, and why.
acceptance_criteria: In frontend/: pnpm run typecheck, pnpm test, pnpm run check:i18n pass; diff -w of old drawer vs article-view.tsx shows only the hook/view seams; drawer click-through unchanged.

title: Docker: run as the fusion user without breaking root-owned volumes
description:
The image runs as root (Dockerfile TODO, upstream f74d2d0) because older /data volumes hold a root-owned fusion.db that the fusion user cannot write. Run as the fusion user without breaking those volumes: a new docker-entrypoint.sh that, when started as root, gives /data to fusion (chown -R) if it is owned by anyone else, then exec su-exec fusion ./refusion. When not started as root (docker run --user), it execs ./refusion directly. Dockerfile: apk add --no-cache su-exec; create fusion with a fixed uid/gid 1000; copy the script; ENTRYPOINT the script; drop the TODO. Keep the Dockerfile diff small: it is an upstream file and upstream merges must stay easy.
Read first: Dockerfile, .dockerignore, scripts.sh (build_backend).
May change: Dockerfile, docker-entrypoint.sh (new), .dockerignore.
Must not change: backend/, frontend/, .github/workflows, anything else.
acceptance_criteria:
Build the binary with ./scripts.sh build-backend linux arm64 build/refusion-linux-arm64 (after ./scripts.sh build-frontend), then docker build. All volumes below are named volumes.
fresh volume -> healthy; ps in the container shows refusion running as uid 1000
volume seeded by a root run (docker run --user 0 --entrypoint ./refusion on the new image, then stop) -> new image starts healthy, files in /data owned 1000:1000, POST /api/sessions with the password returns 2xx
docker run --user 1000:1000 on a 1000-owned volume -> healthy

title: Injected feed CSS: nesting &, existing escapes and control chars broken

escapeCSS in backend/internal/pkg/webpage/css.go (added by 3877517) rewrites & < and non-ASCII runes as CSS hex escapes.
A1: an escaped & is an identifier, so native CSS nesting (.a{& p{}} , &:hover) no longer matches, in preview and web view. Regression: HTML copies worked before.
A2: a backslash already escaping a replaced rune (.a\&b, .caf\é) becomes \\26 , an escaped backslash plus literal text; the rule is lost.
A3: C0 control chars (form feed, U+0001) pass through raw; they are invalid XML 1.0, so an XHTML copy shows a parse error.
Fix idea (not decided): leave & raw in text/html copies; for XHTML copies wrap the style body in /*<![CDATA[*/ ... /*]]>*/ and break any ]]> inside; a backslash before a rune that gets replaced is consumed into the hex escape; form feed becomes a space, other C0 becomes U+FFFD (CSS preprocessing does this for NUL). </ must stay unable to close the style element in HTML.
Files: backend/internal/pkg/webpage/css.go and its tests (webpage.go only if the content type must be passed in). Repro: backend/internal/pkg/webpage/css_escape_repro_test.go.

title: Web view: XHTML copies break; injected CSS not escaped
description:
Found by the 2026-10-13 v4 bug sweep; ledger .research/v4-sweep/findings.md (IDs below). Repro tests are saved under .research/v4-sweep/ at the same paths as in the repo: copy the named ones into place first (they fail today), then fix.
A0: copyAs (backend/internal/pkg/webpage/webpage.go) keeps application/xhtml+xml since the v3 content-type fix, but InjectBase inserts <base href=.. target=_blank> without '/>', so every XHTML copy is malformed XML and the browser shows a parse error instead of the page.

Fix: self-closing base tag (valid in HTML too); escape '&', '<' and every non-ASCII rune in the injected CSS as CSS hex escapes (e.g. \26 , \3c ), which mean the same in CSS and are safe in HTML, XHTML and any charset.

title: Per-feed custom CSS for the web page view
description: A feed can carry custom CSS that is applied to its articles in the web page view, so cluttered sites can be cleaned up (hide sidebars, widen text). The CSS is edited in the feed's settings dialog with a live preview of the feed's newest article.
design:
Decisions, 2026-10-13:

- Mechanism: backend/internal/handler/webpage.go getItemPage redirects frameable sites straight to the origin (cross-origin, no injection possible). When a feed has CSS, the page is always served as a copy, and a <style> block is injected just before </body> (fallback </html>, else appended). "</" in the CSS is escaped. Feeds without CSS are unchanged.
- When CSS is set, <meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy"> tags are stripped from the copy so inline styles are not blocked. The server CSP sandbox header still applies.
- Trade-off accepted: script-heavy sites may break when copied (opaque origin, no cookies). Most framing-blocked sites are already copied today; the preview shows breakage before saving.
- Storage: side table feed_web_css (feed_id PK, cascade delete, css, updated_at), migration 907. Cap 32 KiB. model.Feed untouched.
- Only entry point: a "Web page CSS" row in the edit-feed dialog. No article-view button, no feeds-page or sidebar indicator, no on/off switch, no article picker in the preview.
- Later, not now: enable switch, per-item fetch cache for previews, keeping a draft across accidental close.

title: Store each item's permalink and let a feed open it
description:
Why: link blogs and aggregators point an item at another site, but their
feeds also carry the item's own page on the feed's site in standard fields.
The parser keeps only the main link. Store that own page (permalink) and let
a feed choose to open it.

Read first: backend/internal/pull/parser.go (mapItem, FetchAndParse),
backend/internal/store/item.go (BatchCreateItemsIgnore),
backend/internal/store/migrations/905_feed_default_view.sql and how
default_view flows through model, store, handler and frontend (commit ff6ee06)
- open_permalink follows the same path.

Parser: only when the item's main link host differs from the feed's site host
(feed.SiteURL, else the parsed feed link). Candidates in order: RSS
<comments>, item.Links (Atom links incl. rel="related", RSS atom:link), GUID
if it is an http(s) URL. Take the first whose host is the site host or a
subdomain of it; resolve relative URLs against the base. Else no permalink.
No links from the content. gofeed's universal Item has no comments field:
wrap gofeed.DefaultRSSTranslator via Parser.RSSTranslator and carry
rss.Item.Comments across (e.g. via item.Custom).

Migration 906_item_permalink.sql: items.permalink TEXT NULL;
feeds.open_permalink INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.

Store: keep ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. RowsAffected decides the new-items count,
so DO UPDATE would count every existing item as new. When an insert affects
0 rows and the input has a permalink, run a separate
UPDATE items SET permalink = :permalink
WHERE feed_id = :feed_id AND guid = :guid AND permalink IS NULL.

API: item JSON gains permalink (null when absent); feed JSON gains
open_permalink (bool), accepted on create and update like default_view.
Mirror in frontend/src/lib/api/types.ts.

Use: when the feed's open_permalink is true and the item has a permalink,
GET /items/:id/page, GET /items/:id/full-content and the frontend's open
original link (o/v key, open button) use the permalink; else the main link.
Bookmarks keep keying on the main link.

Frontend: add and edit feed dialogs get "Links open: Linked page / Feed's own
page" next to the default view select; i18n in every locale.

No new keyboard shortcut. Files: anything under backend/ and frontend/src/
needed for the above, except frontend/src/components/ui/ (generated).

Invented examples for tests: site example-news.test; item link
elsewhere.test/story; <comments> example-news.test/item/42; Atom
rel="related" www.example-news.test/linked/7; short link on short.test
(other host, skipped).

title: Mark all read: rows from in-flight and later pages
description: (K4) useMarkScopeRead (frontend/src/queries/items.ts) flips only loadedIds; a next page in flight when the mark starts lands with rows id <= max_id still unread, and settle uses refetchType none, so they stay unread in the list. Fix: the reapply after the in-flight page should flip every unread, unfiltered row with id <= max_id in that scope. (K5) snapshot_id comes from page 1 only, but later pages (backend/internal/handler/item.go listItems) are not bounded by it, so rows with id > snapshot (a newly added feed's backlog with old pub_dates) show on page 2+, flip read optimistically, are skipped by the server and come back unread. Pick the smaller fix: send max_id = max(snapshot, highest loaded id), or have later pages honour the snapshot. description:
What: frontend/src/components/article/article-page.tsx renders <ArticleList /> at a different tree position in panes mode (inside a wrapper div) than in drawer mode (bare). Crossing the breakpoint unmounts and remounts the list: scroll resets to 0, and a stale list query refetches its first page only (pages: 1 in itemQueries.list), so the reader loses their place. Rule (docs/fetch-progress.md, Decisions): the app doesn't move what you're reading unless you asked.
Fix: keep ArticleList at the same tree position in both modes (always render the wrapper, switch its classes; render ArticlePane only in panes mode), so the list and its scroll container survive the switch.

title: Article list: a stale list refetches only its first page
description:
What: when a long list goes stale (a feed check ends, "show new", a filter edit, or a revisit after the 2-minute staleTime), React Query refetches every loaded page one after another: with 500 rows loaded that is 50 requests and 2.5 s on a local server before new articles appear (main thread stays free; the delay is the wait). Refetch only the first page and drop the rest (or cap the number of kept pages), keeping the open article and the scroll position sensible when the list resets.

title: Manage feeds: refresh hidden counts when the feeds list refreshes
description:
The "N hidden" counts on Manage feeds (useHiddenCounts in
frontend/src/queries/feed-filters.ts, GET /filters/hidden-counts) only
refetch on filter events (invalidateFilterViews). A pull that brings in
filtered articles leaves them stale while the page is open.

queryKeys.feeds.all (end of a pull: queries/pull.ts applyPullStatus;

refetches the counts too:
  hiddenCountsKey = [...queryKeys.feeds.all, "hidden-counts"]

(the feeds.all line covers it). Export hiddenCountsKey for the test.

and assert the hidden-counts query is invalidated. It guards the link
between the key and the pull's feeds.all invalidation, which an upstream
merge of pull.ts could break without notice. The test must fail on the old key.

frontend/src/queries/pull.ts (applyPullStatus), frontend/src/store (pull store).

Decisions (2026-10-11):

  * index.css is upstream's file (0x2E/fusion). Its theme block is the part upstream changes most (shadcn regenerations, palette tweaks); editing those lines would conflict on every such upstream merge.
  * The fork rule (.agents/AGENTS.md) is to keep fork changes in new files and leave upstream files minimal. index.css only gains one @import line, a small conflict surface that rarely moves.
  * The fork's colour choices sit in one place, readable at a glance, and undo is clean: delete the file and its import line.
  * Cost: an upstream change to a dark token we override is silently masked. After each upstream merge, diff the .dark block in index.css and decide per token.
  * Selector is `:root.dark`, not `.dark`: imports are hoisted above index.css's own `.dark` block, so a plain `.dark` would lose; the extra specificity wins regardless of order.

title: AI rank: try scoring with a local JevK5 server
description:
What: check that AI ranking works against a self-hosted JevK5 server (open-weight Jev alternative), with nothing sent to OpenRouter.
Why: the scoring service is pluggable (rf-rank-endpoint, FUSION_AI_URL); JevK5 is the known local server speaking the SystemOne shape, but it was never run. Its README example sends `state` as a plain string; we send a JSON object (reader_note, feed_note, article). Unverified whether it accepts that (2026-10-11).
Work in ../refusion-ai-rank (branch ai-rank), DB copy dev-ai-rank.db (it already has the HN note set and feed 25 ranked). Read first: docs/ai-rank.md (Self-hosted scoring), backend/internal/airank/api.go, https://github.com/allebee/jevk5 (README: install, jevk5-serve, POST /v1/systemone).

Steps (ask the user before installing anything or downloading weights: the 4B model is ~9 GB):
1. Install and start JevK5: pip install "jevk5[fast] @ git+https://github.com/allebee/jevk5@v0.3.0", then jevk5-serve --model alibiserikbay/JevK5 --port 8090. On a Mac without a big GPU it may need the GGUF/CPU route from its README; note what worked.
2. One probe with curl: our exact request shape (copy from api.go) to http://localhost:8090/v1/systemone. Record the response shape: does answers.worth.score (0-3) and confidence come back? Is state as an object accepted?
3. Run the branch backend with FUSION_AI_URL=http://localhost:8090/v1/systemone and no FUSION_AI_API_KEY, port 8081, FUSION_DB_PATH=dev-ai-rank.db. Wait for one run. Stop the backend afterwards (it must not keep ranking).
4. Compare its groups for feed 25 with the OpenRouter run recorded in rf-rank-endpoint's comment (love 3 / related 15 / neutral 14 / skip 14): same top and bottom?

If state as an object is refused or scores are nonsense: report the response, propose the smallest fix (e.g. a FUSION_AI_STATE_FORMAT or serializing state to text for such services) as a new bead; don't build it here.
Not in scope: changing the default service, packaging JevK5, docs beyond a short "tested with" note in docs/ai-rank.md if it works.
acceptance_criteria:
- curl probe response recorded in a bead comment (shape, score, latency per decision)
- /api/ai-rank/status with FUSION_AI_URL only: available true, service localhost:8090, error null, scored_today > 0
- group counts for feed 25 compared with the OpenRouter run, in a bead comment
- test backend and jevk5-serve stopped afterwards

title: Search index: plain text, external content, no re-index on mark-read
description:
Why: items_fts (backend/internal/store/migrations/001_initial.sql:48-73) has three faults:
 a) the update trigger is AFTER UPDATE ON items, so every unread toggle
    re-indexes the item and MarkAllAsRead (store/item.go:248) re-indexes the
    whole table;
 b) it indexes raw HTML, so searching a tag/attribute name ("div", "href") or
    a link's domain matches markup;
 c) it is a contentful FTS5 table, storing a second copy of every title and
    content.
yarr fixed all three (migrations m14_upgrade_fts5 and m15 in
github.com/nkanaev/yarr src/storage/sqlite/migration.go).

What:
1. New file backend/internal/store/fts.go: register a deterministic SQLite
   scalar function strip_html(text) in a package init() via modernc's
   sqlite.RegisterDeterministicScalarFunction, so every connection has it,
   including the legacy-migration path (migrate_legacy.go). It returns visible text:
   drops tags and <script>/<style> bodies, decodes entities, puts a space
   at block boundaries so words don't merge. Use golang.org/x/net/html
   (already an indirect dep; go mod tidy makes it direct).
2. New migration backend/internal/store/migrations/901_fts_plain_text.sql
   (fork numbering, see .agents/AGENTS.md): drop items_fts and its three
   triggers; recreate items_fts as fts5(title, content, content='items',
   content_rowid='id', tokenize='unicode61'); recreate triggers with the
   same names: insert, delete (FTS5 'delete' command passing
   strip_html(old.content)), and update as AFTER UPDATE OF title, content;
   repopulate with INSERT ... SELECT id, title, strip_html(content) FROM items.
3. docs/backend-design.md:52: one line saying items_fts indexes stripped
   text over external content, and why (no copy, no re-index on mark-read).

Gotchas (put the first two in a <=3-line SQL comment in 901):
- The delete command must receive exactly the values that were indexed, so
  strip_html must stay deterministic; changing it later needs a re-index.
- Never run FTS5 'rebuild' on this table: it would read raw HTML from items.
- Editing items.title/content from the sqlite3 CLI will fail ("no such
  function: strip_html"). Accepted.
- SearchItems (store/item.go:408) and the API stay unchanged.

Files: may add fts.go, 901_fts_plain_text.sql, fts_test.go; may change
go.mod/go.sum and docs/backend-design.md. Must not change 001_initial.sql,
store.go, item.go or other upstream files.

title: Proxy: decide whether to honour HTTP_PROXY for feeds without their own proxy
description:
Background: since upstream's refactor ad25dde the feed dialogs said an empty proxy field uses the system proxy, but refusion never read HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY: httpc NewClient (backend/internal/pkg/httpc/client.go) builds its own http.Transport with no Proxy func, so empty means direct. rf-pause-proxy-text corrected the hint to say so (2026-10-13).
Open question: should the server honour the standard env proxy variables (http.ProxyFromEnvironment) when a feed has no proxy of its own? Catch: the private-address guard (publicOnlyControl, set on the dialer only when proxyURL is empty) would then check the proxy's address, not the feed's, because net/http dials the proxy. Honouring env proxies means deciding how that guard works with them (trust the env proxy like a per-feed one, or resolve the target first), plus NO_PROXY handling and the cache key in NewClient.
Decide first whether anyone needs it; if yes, write the plan here before building.
Files if built: backend/internal/pkg/httpc/client.go and its test, .env.example, the proxy hint in frontend/src/lib/i18n/messages/, docs/using.md.
acceptance_criteria: a decision recorded in this bead; if built: a feed with an empty proxy field fetches through HTTP_PROXY in a test, and the private-address guard still blocks a private target

title: Mark rollback: older pending mark ignored; scope partial failure un-reads server-read rows
description:
Found by the 2026-10-13 v5 bug sweep; ledger .research/v5-sweep/findings.md (IDs below). Repro tests are saved under .research/v5-sweep/ at the same paths as in the repo (also in the working tree, uncommitted): they fail today; make them pass, then commit them with the fix.
C1: revertValue in frontend/src/queries/items.ts returns entry.confirmed for the newest mark, even when an older mark on the same row is still pending. Row unread; mark read A pending; mark unread B fails; A succeeds -> row shows unread, server has it read, count and row disagree until a list refetch. Correct: revert to the target of the newest older mark still pending, else to confirmed. (read A + read B, B fails first, does not reproduce: B flips nothing.)

title: Mark read: don't wait for /feeds, don't cancel list pages, skip untouched lists
description:
What: three costs in the mark-read mutation (CPU per mark is small, 16-32 ms; this is about requests and lost work):
- useSetItemsReadState onSettled awaits a full /feeds refetch, so the mutation stays pending until it returns, though the optimistic update already set the unread counts.
- onMutate cancels every items query (queryKeys.items.all), which can discard an in-flight next-page load.
- applyOptimisticItemReadState rebuilds every page of every cached list, even lists that don't hold the item.
Make mark-read settle without waiting for /feeds (refetch in the background or only on error), cancel only what the optimistic update overwrites, and return unchanged cache entries untouched.

Read first: frontend/src/queries/items.ts (useSetItemsReadState, useMarkScopeRead, applyOptimisticItemReadState, snapshot helpers), hooks/use-auto-mark-read.ts (hasPendingMutation retry), queries/keys.ts.
May change: queries/items.ts and its tests. Unread counts must still end correct after errors (rollback).
acceptance_criteria:
